witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K1); but for the Quadripartitus and the London texts Liebermann’s K means Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 51.7c
div.ab: Et si alicuius precepto namium excusserint, qui in eos potestatem haberet, omnes simul unam forisfacturam reddant; sicut acciderint, singillatim componant.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 573 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: verderbt etwa aus si secus acciderit: für Pfandkehrung, die nicht Einer befohlen, zahlen sie einzeln Strafgeld
corrupt, perhaps from si secus acciderit: for a rescue of a distress not ordered by one man, they pay fines individually
Vgl. Gl gemeinschaftliche Missetat 12—-rit{44}—sig.{46}—51, 8 Am Rande spät: Qualiter excussio namii id est districtionis fieri poterit Rs
Cf. Gl gemeinschaftliche Missetat 12—-rit{44}—sig.{46}—51, 8 in the margin, in a late hand: Qualiter excussio namii id est districtionis fieri poterit Rs

div.ab: And if they have rescued a distress at the command of someone who had power over them, let them all together pay one fine; as [the offences] came about, let them make terms separately [?].
